title: AgentOS workspace lifecycle and control center
summary: An authenticated owner reaches the exact ready AgentOS workspace, securely opens OpenClaw or n8n as independent post-ready app launches, runs auditable workspace operations with explicit safety boundaries, and observes or reindexes the internal MCP-Qdrant knowledge runtime without receiving infrastructure credentials.

includes: AgentOS catalogue request and exact-order resume
Wallet as the linked-invoice payment waypoint
Workspace provisioning and the exact workspace as the primary terminal
Solution module detail as an optional post-ready workspace branch
Secure OpenClaw and n8n launch as optional app-bound post-ready branches
Public owner-scoped update, paid plan change, verified backup, non-destructive restart and confirmed rebuild operations
MCP-Qdrant runtime health, safe knowledge summary and asynchronous reindexing inside the exact workspace
Application launch, workspace operation and knowledge runtime as independent block state axes
excludes: Treating module detail or OpenClaw launch as required provisioning stages
Wallet top-up, provider settlement and invoice anatomy owned by nivo/wallet-billing
Destructive data reset or wipe under the Restart action
Applying a plan change before its linked adjustment invoice is paid
Reusable application or Qdrant credentials, Qdrant admin routes, raw document text, point identifiers and control-plane semantic search

rules.statement: Wallet is the payment waypoint for the invoice linked to the exact AgentOS order, and completion returns the owner to that same order context.
The primary journey terminates at /[locale]/agentos/workspaces/[workspaceId] for the exact workspace that fulfilled the order.
Module detail and OpenClaw launch are optional branches available only after the exact workspace is ready; neither is a required provisioning stage.
Workspace provisioning and OpenClaw launch are independent state axes; a launch transition never changes the workspace lifecycle state.
Workspace lifecycle is reconciled from owner-scoped order, invoice and workspace facts, with the later workspace fact taking precedence.
OpenClaw access uses short-lived issue, renew and revoke operations and never exposes reusable credentials.
OpenClaw launch requires an active exact workspace, active instance and ready runtime; module post-ready sequencing remains owner intent until an equivalent guard exists.
n8n uses the same short-lived app-bound issue, renew and revoke security boundary as OpenClaw and never exposes a reusable credential.
Update, plan change, backup, restart and rebuild are exact-owner-scoped asynchronous operations with explicit accepted, running, succeeded and refused results.
Restart is the non-destructive recovery action and preserves persistent workspace data; no action labelled Restart may reset or wipe data.
A plan change creates an exact adjustment order and linked Wallet invoice and is applied only after that invoice is paid.
Backup reports success only after verification; rebuild requires explicit confirmation and a fresh verified backup before the release is replaced without deleting persistent volumes.

MCP and Qdrant remain internal runtime components; the owner may receive health, document counts by origin, last update and reindex state, but no credential, raw text, point id, admin route or control-plane semantic search.
Application launch, workspace operation and knowledge reindex transitions are independent block state axes and never redefine workspace lifecycle or page anatomy.

acceptance.statement: Creating an AgentOS order establishes /[locale]/agentos/orders/[orderId] as the exact resumable journey context.
The Wallet waypoint identifies and pays the invoice linked to that exact order and exposes a return to the same order rather than choosing an unrelated unpaid invoice.
When provisioning resolves a ready workspaceId, the primary action opens /[locale]/agentos/workspaces/[workspaceId], not the generic AgentOS index.
Module detail and OpenClaw launch are reachable only as optional branches from a ready exact workspace and are absent from required primary progress.
Launch idle, opening, connected, blocked, expired and disconnected transitions remain independent from request, payment, provisioning and workspace readiness states.
Update, plan change, backup, restart and rebuild controls become runnable only through their corresponding public owner-scoped backend operations and expose real pending, success and refusal states.
A ready exact workspace can issue, renew and revoke n8n launch with the same app-bound short-lived security and independent launch state used by OpenClaw.
Restart preserves persistent data; backup verifies its artifact; rebuild requires explicit confirmation plus a fresh verified backup and never masquerades as Restart.
Plan change returns an exact adjustment order and linked Wallet invoice and does not apply the new plan until payment succeeds.
Infrastructure exposes MCP and Qdrant health, knowledge document counts by origin, last update and reindex state without credentials, raw text, point ids, admin routes or control-plane search.
Launch, operation and knowledge reindex conditions render as block states inside the existing workspace page architecture; they do not become page states unless page anatomy changes.

evidence.claim: The owner standardizes Wallet as the payment waypoint, the exact workspace as the primary terminal, module detail and OpenClaw as post-ready branches, and launch as an independent state axis.
The frontend reconciles exact owner order, invoice and workspace facts into separate order and workspace lifecycle phases, with the later workspace fact taking precedence.
Ordering establishes the exact resume URL and awaiting-payment opens Wallet, while the current ready action still targets the generic AgentOS index.
Wallet renders owner invoices and currently pays the first unpaid invoice without receiving exact AgentOS order or invoice identity.
The frontend publishes a control-center route bound to one exact workspaceId.
Solution module detail is nested beneath the exact workspace and binds both workspaceId and installationId.
OpenClaw launch is an exact-workspace launch bridge route outside the required provisioning surface.
The workspace snapshot and OpenClaw issue, renew, revoke and broadcast lifecycle are held as separate frontend state owners.
Solutions and OpenClaw applications are peer branches within the answered exact workspace control center rather than provisioning stages.
The backend exposes one exact viewer-owned AgentOS control-center aggregate.
The install mutation binds the authenticated owner and exact workspace to the requested solution installation.
Issue launch is exact-owner scoped and refuses non-AgentOS, inactive workspace or instance, missing hostname, unavailable capability and unready runtime before returning a credential-free launch.
OpenClaw access uses a hashed one-use grant and owner-scoped short-lived Redis lease with independent redeem, renew, revoke and validate behavior.
The authenticated orderCatalogItem operation creates the catalogue order and linked invoice but does not itself provision AgentOS.
The authenticated payInvoice operation settles one exact invoice by invoiceId and returns its updated payment state.

Supersede the current in-progress AgentOS workspace scope so a later accepted intent can add secure n8n launch, public owner-scoped workspace operations, and owner-safe MCP-Qdrant knowledge runtime without reusable credentials.
The committed frontend names update, plan, backup, reset and rebuild but deliberately disables every action because no public operation is wired.
The current app-bound launch contract contains only OpenClaw, proving n8n launch requires an explicit backend capability expansion rather than credential reuse.
The current owner-scoped workspace aggregate marks n8n unavailable with SECURITY_UPGRADE_REQUIRED while exposing its observed version.
The internal rebuild capability requires acknowledgement, takes and verifies a fresh backup, refuses without verified backup, uninstalls only the release and dispatches reinstall.
The backend defines an owner-safe Qdrant knowledge summary of document count, origins and last update while explicitly excluding raw text, search and identifiers.
AgentOS provisioning already declares n8n, MCP and Qdrant runtime components and bounded resources inside the workspace chart.
Installed agents already receive an internal MCP server binding with per-agent capability headers, proving MCP is runtime infrastructure rather than an owner credential.

The owner accepts a pending AgentOS workspace expansion: secure app-bound n8n launch; public owner-scoped update, paid plan change, verified backup, non-destructive restart and confirmed rebuild operations; and owner-safe MCP-Qdrant health, knowledge summary and reindexing without reusable credentials, raw document access, point identifiers, admin routes or control-plane semantic search.
